# git maintenance

Git commands that **add** data (`add`, `commit`, `fetch`) optimize for a snappy UI. They do not spend time reshaping the whole object database. [`git maintenance`](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-maintenance) is the operator tool that runs background (or manual) **optimization tasks**: commit-graph, prefetch, loose-object packing, multi-pack-index repacks, and more — without turning every `git status` into a full `gc`.

## Mental model

```text
foreground Git  ──► writes packs / loose objects / refs  (fast path)
        │
        ▼
git maintenance run / start
        │
        ├── commit-graph      (faster reachability / log)
        ├── prefetch          (objects ready before real fetch)
        ├── loose-objects     (loose → pack, carefully)
        ├── incremental-repack (multi-pack-index dance)
        └── pack-refs, …      (ref iteration speed)
```

`git maintenance start` registers the repo and installs a **scheduler** (systemd user timers on modern Linux, else cron; launchctl / schtasks on macOS / Windows). `register` alone updates config; `start` = register + schedule.

## Tasks that matter at scale

| Task | What it does | Default under `incremental` strategy |
|------|----------------|--------------------------------------|
| `commit-graph` | Incremental commit-graph write + verify; safe beside concurrent Git | hourly |
| `prefetch` | `git fetch` into `refs/prefetch/` (no tag update; does not move remote-tracking branches) | hourly |
| `loose-objects` | Delete loose objects already packed; pack a batch of remaining loose objects | daily |
| `incremental-repack` | `multi-pack-index expire` then `repack` small packs into a larger one | daily |
| `pack-refs` | Pack loose refs into a single file | weekly (when enabled by strategy) |
| `gc` | Full garbage collection / aggressive repack — **expensive**; not on the incremental schedule | manual / other strategies |

Prefetch makes the **next** interactive `git fetch` mostly a tip update when objects were already downloaded. Exclude a remote with `remote.<name>.skipFetchAll` if that remote should not be prefetched.

`incremental-repack` uses the **multi-pack-index (MIDX)**: expire unreferenced packs, then repack a batch of small packs and retarget MIDX entries. Default batch size `0` means “try to fold into one pack.”

## Worked examples

### Case 1: One-shot tasks on a lab clone

```bash
cd /path/to/large-repo

# Inspect whether auto thresholds say work is due
git maintenance is-needed --auto; echo "exit=$?"

# Run specific safe tasks explicitly
git maintenance run --task=commit-graph
git maintenance run --task=loose-objects
git maintenance run --task=incremental-repack

# Optional: see commit-graph files appear
ls -la .git/objects/info/commit-graph 2>/dev/null || ls -la .git/objects/info/commit-graphs/ 2>/dev/null || true
```

Use `--task` when you want a known order. Without `--task`, Git runs tasks with `maintenance.<task>.enabled=true` (by default that is mainly `gc` unless you set a strategy).

### Case 2: Enable incremental strategy and register

```bash
cd /path/to/large-repo

git maintenance register
# Sets maintenance.strategy=incremental if unset, adds repo to global maintenance.repo,
# enables recommended schedules, sets maintenance.auto=false in this repo

git config --get maintenance.strategy
git config --get-all --global maintenance.repo | tail -n 5
git config --get maintenance.auto
```

Expected shape: `incremental`, a path entry under `maintenance.repo`, and `maintenance.auto=false` so foreground commands do not also kick auto-maintenance while the scheduler owns the job.

### Case 3: `git maintenance start` on Linux

```bash
cd /path/to/large-repo
git maintenance start --scheduler=auto
# On Linux with user systemd: systemd-timer; otherwise crontab

systemctl --user list-timers 'git-maintenance*' 2>/dev/null || true
# Or: crontab -l | sed -n '/GIT MAINTENANCE/,/END GIT MAINTENANCE/p'
```

Timers run `git for-each-repo --config=maintenance.repo maintenance run --schedule=hourly|daily|weekly`. Stop with `git maintenance stop` (leaves the repo registered). `unregister` removes the repo from the global list (`--force` if unsure).

### Case 4: Prefetch vs a normal fetch

```bash
# After maintenance has run prefetch on a registered remote:
git show-ref | grep prefetch | head
git fetch origin
# Ideal case: tips move with little or no object transfer
```

Prefetch refs live under `refs/prefetch/` so your `origin/main` does not jump until **you** fetch.

### Case 5: Manual vs scheduled, and locks

```bash
# Manual full gc via maintenance (preferred over bare git gc when using the framework)
git maintenance run --task=gc

# Auto mode: only if thresholds say so (loose object count, pack count, …)
git maintenance run --auto
```

Each `git maintenance run` takes an **object database lock**. Overlapping hourly runs on huge multi-repo schedules can skip a cycle — shrink task cost or stagger repos if windows exceed an hour. Do not mix bare `git gc` with concurrent `git maintenance run`; prefer `git maintenance run --task=gc`.

## Strategy cheat sheet

| `maintenance.strategy` | Intent |
|------------------------|--------|
| `none` | Scheduled maintenance runs nothing by default |
| `gc` | Run the `gc` task |
| `geometric` | Geometric pack repack + auxiliary cleanup; strong default for **manual** maintenance on large repos (Git 2.50+ docs) |
| `incremental` | Small non-deleting tasks on a schedule; manual path still uses `gc` |

Tune with `maintenance.<task>.enabled` and `maintenance.<task>.schedule` (`hourly` / `daily` / `weekly`). Threshold knobs include `maintenance.commit-graph.auto`, `maintenance.loose-objects.auto`, `maintenance.incremental-repack.auto`.

## Safety

- Prefetch contacts remotes on a timer — ensure credentials/agents work non-interactively or exclude remotes.
- `gc` deletes stale data; incremental tasks prefer not to. Know which strategy you enabled before leaving a laptop on a huge monorepo overnight.
- Customizing systemd units: use drop-ins under `~/.config/systemd/user/git-maintenance@.service.d/`; `start` overwrites the main unit files.
- `maintenance.auto=false` after `register` is intentional; re-enable only if you understand double scheduling.

## Hands-on checklist

1. On a disposable clone, run `commit-graph` and `incremental-repack` with `--task`.
2. `git maintenance register` and confirm `maintenance.strategy` / `maintenance.repo`.
3. `git maintenance start`; list timers or crontab region.
4. Trigger prefetch; inspect `refs/prefetch/`; run a normal `git fetch` and note transfer size.
5. `git maintenance stop` and `unregister` when the lab is done.

## Pitfalls

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---------|--------------|-----|
| Hourly tasks sometimes skip | Overlap on object DB lock | Fewer repos per user, cheaper tasks, or longer spacing |
| Remote-tracking branches “randomly” move | Not prefetch — something else fetching | Prefetch should only touch `refs/prefetch/` |
| Disk grows after incremental mode | No full `gc`; MIDX keeps more packs briefly | Periodic manual `gc` / geometric strategy if policy allows |
| Scheduler missing on Linux | No user systemd / lingering | `loginctl enable-linger $USER` or use `--scheduler=crontab` |
| `unregister` errors | Repo not in list | `git maintenance unregister --force` |
